data.q: What does the `NonNullable<T>` utility type do?
Which utility type makes all properties of an object type optional?
data.e: `Partial<T>` sets every property of `T` to optional.

data.q: What is the result of `{ a: number } & { b: string }`?
data.e: Intersection types combine members of both types, resulting in an object with both properties.

data.q: How do you extract the return type of a function type `T`?
data.e: `ReturnType<T>` infers the return type of a function type `T`.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `infer` keyword in a conditional type?
o: To declare a new generic type parameter
To capture and reference a type within the conditional branch
To enforce a constraint on a generic
To create a union of all possible types
data.e: `infer` allows you to declare a type variable that captures a portion of a type for use in the true branch.

data.q: Which mapped type makes all properties of a type readonly?
data.e: `Readonly<T>` sets the `readonly` modifier on every property of `T`.

data.q: What is a key difference between `type` aliases and `interface` declarations in TypeScript?
o: Type aliases support declaration merging, interfaces do not
Interfaces support declaration merging, type aliases do not
Type aliases cannot represent primitive types
data.e: Interfaces can be merged automatically when declared multiple times; type aliases cannot.

data.q: What does `keyof T` produce for an object type `T`?
o: A tuple of all property values
A union of all property keys (as string literals)
The type of the first property
data.e: `keyof T` yields a union of string literal types representing the keys of `T`.

data.q: Which utility type constructs a new type by picking a set of properties `K` from `T`?
data.e: `Pick<T, K>` selects only the properties `K` from `T`.

o: A value that can be any type
A value that never occurs (e.g., function that always throws)
data.e: `never` is the type for values that never happen, such as a function that throws or never returns.

data.q: How can you create a type that requires at least one property from a union of object types?
o: Use a discriminated union with a common required property
data.e: A discriminated union with a shared required property (e.g., a `type` field) ensures at least one variant is present.

data.q: What is the result of `type Flatten<T> = T extends any[] ? T[number] : T;` when `T` is `string[]`?
data.e: The conditional type checks if `T` is an array; if so, it returns the element type (`string`).

data.q: Which utility type removes `readonly` and `?` modifiers from all properties of `T`?
data.e: `Required<T>` makes all properties required and removes `readonly`.
